rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the brothers testified to the theft only on the basis of what they knew.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد بقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they knew the rule that a thief would be seized and enslaved, after Jacob asked how the ruler knew this.
rows.anchor: ما شهدنا عند العزيز أن السارق يؤخذ بسرقته ويسترق إلا بما علمنا من حكم المسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the first interpretation as the closer fit to context.
rows.anchor: وأقرب المعنيين إلى السياق أولهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading is that they had not foreseen the theft and seizure and had relied on appearances when taking Benjamin along.
rows.anchor: لم نكن نعلم أن ابنك سيسرق فيؤخذ ويسترق وإنما كنا نعتمد على ظاهر الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen means Benjamin's unknown theft of the cup and impending seizure; they could not have known so as to withhold testimony.
rows.anchor: والحق أن المراد بالغيب كونه سارقا مع جهلهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village is apparently Egypt; the caravan is the party traveling with them, whose members witnessed the affair and could dispel Jacob's doubt.
rows.anchor: وبالعير التي أقبلوا فيها القافلة التي كانوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to question the witnesses assures Jacob they did not neglect Benjamin: he really stole and was enslaved.
rows.anchor: لإزالة الريب من نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage recounts Jacob's response after his sons' second return and his sending them back to seek Joseph and Benjamin.
rows.anchor: تتضمن محاورة يعقوب بنيه بعد رجوعهم ثانيا من مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transition is omitted: after the sons returned and repeated their eldest brother's instruction, Jacob replied with these words.
rows.anchor: والتقدير ولما رجعوا إلى أبيهم وقالوا ما وصاهم به كبيرهم قال أبوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob was not calling his sons liars, since their report had truthful signs and was open to verification.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل عليه السلام هذا القول تكذيبا لهم فيما أخبروه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By divine insight he sensed this calamity, like Joseph's earlier one, arose from their self-directed scheming.
rows.anchor: وجد بفراسة إلهية أن هذه الواقعة ترتبط وتتفرع على تسويل نفساني منهم إجمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His hope that God return them all includes Joseph, Benjamin, and the eldest brother left in Egypt.
rows.anchor: فجمع في ذلك بين يوسف وأخيه وكبير الإخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the interpretation that Jacob merely doubted them and conjectured they had devised another matter.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن قولهم إن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob expresses hope rather than prayer; he expects Joseph alive and hopes patience will bring all three sons back and complete God's favor.
rows.anchor: بل هو رجاء لثمرة الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All-Knowing and All-Wise explain God's knowledge of whom to choose and His wise completion of favor; hardship should not prompt agitation or despair.
rows.anchor: إنه هو العليم بمورد الاجتباء وإتمام النعمة حكيم في فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names All-Knowing and All-Wise first appear in Jacob's words to Joseph about his dream and later in Joseph's words at reunion.
rows.anchor: ذكرهما يعقوب ليوسف عليهما السلام لأول مرة أول رؤياه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says asaf can mean grief and anger together, or either alone, describing the heart surging with desire for revenge.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الأسف الحزن والغضب معا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says anger spreads toward someone lower, while grief contracts in response to someone higher.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الأسف الحزن والغضب معا، وقد يقال لكل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā says God does not grieve as humans do; His friends' pleasure and anger are treated as His, and insulting a friend is like declaring war on God.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يأسف كأسفنا ولكن له أولياء يأسفون ويرضون فجعل رضاهم رضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāẓim means holding breath or silence; it also describes restraining anger, a camel stopping rumination, and a tied full waterskin.
rows.anchor: والكظوم احتباس النفس ويعبر به عن السكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whitening means loss of sight, confirmed by the later instruction to put Joseph's shirt on Jacob's face so he would see again.
rows.anchor: يشهد بأنه كناية عن ذهاب البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turns away, grieves for Joseph, loses sight from grief, and suppresses anger and sorrow without acting against his sons.
rows.anchor: حابس غيظه متجرع حزنه لا يتعرض لبنيه بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍ means nearing death; another view says neither dead and forgotten nor alive and hoped for. The first fits the contrast with perishing; it is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الحرض والحارض المشرف على الهلاك وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons say Jacob will keep remembering Joseph until he approaches death or dies.
rows.anchor: لا تزال تذكر يوسف وتديم ذكره منذ سنين لا تكف عنه حتى تشرف على الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement may express tenderness and pity; the author also suspects irritation and weariness with his long weeping, which seemed to accuse them.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قولهم هذا أنهم إنما قالوه رقة بحاله ورأفة به

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines bathth as an uncontainable worry that its bearer spreads; the word means what has been broadcast.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع البث الهم الذي لا يقدر صاحبه على كتمانه فيبثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is a reversal: Jacob says he is not complaining to his family, since ordinary human grief shared with people soon dissipates.
rows.anchor: من قصر القلب فيكون مفاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He complains only to God, who never tires of requests; his knowledge from God means he does not despair of relief or mercy.
rows.anchor: ولا يأخذه ملل ولا سأمة فيما يسأله عنه عباده

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines taḥassus as seeking by the senses and reports that it and tajassus can be synonyms paired for verbal variation, with poetry as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع التحسس - بالحاء - طلب الشيء بالحاسة

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Another distinction is that tajassus searches for people's faults while taḥassus listens to a group's conversation.
rows.anchor: وقيل التجسس بالجيم البحث عن عورات الناس، وبالحاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says taḥassus seeks good, while tajassus seeks evil.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عن الفرق بينهما؟ قال لا يبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūḥ literally means breath or soul and metaphorically relief after constriction; God's relief is an opening after hardship by His will.
rows.anchor: فالروح المنسوب إليه تعالى هو الفرج بعد الشدة بإذن الله ومشيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must trust God's unconquerable will; despair of His relief limits His power and mercy and approaches disbelief.
rows.anchor: وليس له أن ييأس من روح الله ويقنط من رحمته فإنه تحديد لقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob tells his sons to search for Joseph and Benjamin, detained in Egypt, and not despair of relief after hardship.
rows.anchor: والفرج الذي يرزقه الله بعد الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who do not believe God can remove every grief and distress despair of His relief.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يؤمنون بأن الله يقدر أن يكشف كل غمة وينفس عن كل كربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meager barter is little merchandise; the account omits the brothers' journey to Egypt before their plea.
rows.anchor: البضاعة المزجاة المتاع القليل، وفي الكلام حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lack enough money for food, have been branded thieves, and Joseph had refused to release Benjamin, so ordinary means offer little hope.
rows.anchor: إحداهما أن يبيع منهم الطعام ولا ثمن عندهم يفي بما يريدونه من الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They humble themselves by describing distress, then their meager goods, then asking for a full measure and charity.
rows.anchor: فذكروا أولا ما مسهم وأهلهم من الضر وسوء الحال ثم ذكروا قلة ما أتوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their charitable appeal indirectly asks Joseph to free Benjamin, treated outwardly as his property; its close is a prayer for reward.
rows.anchor: وأما حديث أخيهم المأخوذ فلم يصرحوا بسؤال تخلية سبيله بل سألوه أن يتصدق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises Joseph and Benjamin while humbling their brothers for wrongdoing; Joseph reveals himself then though he could have told them earlier.
rows.anchor: أنه سيرفع يوسف وأخاه ويضع عنده سائر بني يعقوب لظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers stand humiliated before Joseph, with their envied brother beside him in power.
rows.anchor: أن يوقف إخوته أمامه ومعه أخوه المحسود موقف المذلة والمسكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's words link to Abraham's saying that only the misguided despair of their Lord's mercy; reports count such despair a ruinous major sin.
rows.anchor: وقد عد اليأس من روح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' charge of Jacob's old error meant excessive love for Joseph: they thought their father favored two young sons over them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن مرادهم بالضلال ههنا هو مرادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not mean religious misguidance or disbelief; their words show they followed the monotheistic religion of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: يشهد على أنهم كانوا موحدين على دين آبائهم إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer of good news carried Joseph's shirt; Joseph's question recalls his earlier claim to know from God what his family did not.
rows.anchor: البشير حامل البشارة وكان حامل القميص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons seek forgiveness for their deeds against Joseph and Benjamin; Joseph had already forgiven them.
rows.anchor: وأما يوسف فقد كان استغفر لهم قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob postpones prayer, as sawfa indicates, perhaps until reunion with Joseph has fully healed the traces of separation.
rows.anchor: ولعله إنما أخره ليتم له النعمة بلقاء يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports say Jacob delayed until a time when prayer is answered.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار إنه أخره إلى وقت يستجاب فيه الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits Jacob and his family leaving their land and traveling to Egypt before arriving at Joseph.
rows.anchor: في الكلام حذف والتقدير فخرج يعقوب وآله من أرضهم وساروا إلى مصر

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes differ whether the parents were Joseph's biological father and mother or Jacob and Joseph's aunt, on the view his mother died when he was young.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون مختلفون في أنهما كانا والديه أباه وأمه أو أنهما يعقوب وزوجه خالة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an supports neither possibility expressly, but the apparent meaning of parents is his actual parents.
rows.anchor: ولا يوجد في كلامه تعالى ما يؤيد أحد المحتملين غير أن الظاهر من الأبوين هما الحقيقيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph embraces his parents and invites the family into Egypt; the account places their meeting outside the city.
rows.anchor: أي أبواه وإخوته وأهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne is a raised seat commonly used by a king; kharr means falling to the ground, and badw is the open country where Jacob lived.
rows.anchor: العرش هو السرير العالي ويكثر استعماله فيما يجلس عليه الملك ويختص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family likely settled in the room before Joseph entered; context suggests attendants had seated his parents, and the prostration came at first sight of Joseph.
rows.anchor: فكأنهم دخلوا البيت واطمأن بهم المجلس ثم دخل عليهم يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration's pronoun refers to Joseph; the alternative that it refers to God has no support in the wording.
rows.anchor: لا دليل عليه من جهة اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was not worship of Joseph: Jacob and Joseph were monotheists, and the family treated him as God's sign and direction, like the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: فليس المعبود عندها إلا الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects explanations that prostration was a greeting, a then-permitted act of honor, or a bow-like pose.
rows.anchor: وقول بعضهم كان سجودهم كهيئة الركوع كما يفعله الأعاجم كل ذلك غير وجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family recognized fulfillment of Joseph's childhood dream of eleven stars, the sun, and the moon bowing to him.
rows.anchor: ذكر الرؤيا التى رأى فيها أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر له ساجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph thanks God for release from prison, a hardship turned into a means of honor and kingship; out of generosity he tactfully omits the pit before his brothers.
rows.anchor: فذكر إحسان ربه به في إخراجه من السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He alludes to the pit as Satan's provocation, which caused separation; God then brought him prosperity and reunited the family from the desert.
rows.anchor: وقد أحسن بي من بعد أن أفسد الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's subtle care turned hardship, abasement, and servitude into ease, honor, and kingship; al-Laṭīf encompasses hidden things.
rows.anchor: نفذ فيها فجعل عوامل الشدة عوامل رخاء وراحة وأسباب الذلة والرقية وسائل عزة وملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of laṭīf conveys smallness, fineness, and penetration through tiny passages, and by extension gentleness.
rows.anchor: والأصل في معناه الصغر والدقة والنفوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All-Knowing and All-Wise explain the preceding account and echo the names Jacob used interpreting Joseph's first dream.
rows.anchor: وقد علل عليه السلام الكلام وختمه بهذين الاسمين محاذاة لأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting God's gifts, Joseph turns from his father to address God, naming kingship and knowledge of interpreting reports.
rows.anchor: لما أثنى عليه السلام على ربه وعد ما دفع عنه من الشدائد والنوائب أراد أن يذكر ما خصه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Creator of the heavens and earth advances praise to universal guardianship in both worlds, grounded in God's originating all things.
rows.anchor: إضراب وترق في الثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine guardianship means God originates and sustains every thing's essence, qualities, and acts, so devoted hearts turn to Him as Creator.
rows.anchor: وولايته تعالى أعني كونه قائما كل شيء في ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله منشؤها إيجاده تعالى إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God as Creator is Joseph's sole guardian; Joseph has no independent power over his self, benefit, harm, life, or resurrection.
rows.anchor: إني تحت ولايتك التامة من غير أن يكون لي صنع في نفسي واستقلال في ذاتي وصفاتي وأفعالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To die Muslim asks for Islam throughout life, then for entry among the righteous in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وهو الإسلام ما دام حيا في الدنيا والدخول في زمرة الصالحين في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A perfect servant submits to God's will in life and becomes fit for nearness and gifts in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ولا يظهر منه ما يكرهه ولا يرتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Islam Joseph asks for is the highest surrender, in which the servant sees no independent self or efficacy apart from God.
rows.anchor: وهو التسليم المحض لله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Die Muslim means asking God to preserve sincerity until life's end, not asking to die or to die Muslim after a prior non-Muslim life.
rows.anchor: أن يعيش مسلما حتى يتوفاه الله فهو كناية عن أن يثبته الله على الإسلام حتى يموت

rows.speaker: عدة من قدماء المفسرين
rows.claim: Some early exegetes read these words as a request for death; one said Joseph alone among prophets asked or wished for death.
rows.anchor: دعاء منه يسأل به الموت من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the early exegetes' reading that Joseph requested death.
rows.anchor: ويتبين بذلك فساد ما روي عن عدة من قدماء المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen account is Joseph's story, the address is to Muhammad, and the plural refers to Joseph's brothers plotting their decision.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijmaʿ means resolve; the Prophet's absence is a circumstantial clause explaining how this is unseen revelation.
rows.anchor: والإجماع العزم والإرادة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir reports that Joseph sent his tear-soaked shirt, whose scent restored Jacob's sight; the brothers traveled nine days, Jacob smelled Joseph, regained sight, and asked about Benjamin.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث طويل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the throne is a bed and the family's prostration was worship of God.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir reports Joseph embraced Jacob, seated his aunt on the royal bed, returned in royal dress, and the family prostrated in gratitude; Joseph abstained from grooming and women during their twenty years apart.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث قال فسار تسعة أيام

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā says Joseph wore silk with gold and ruled among Pharaoh's people; they needed his justice, while an Imam must be truthful, keep promises, and judge fairly. Lawful food and dress are not forbidden.
rows.anchor: عن العباس بن هلال الشامي مولى أبي الحسن عليه السلام عنه قول قلت له جعلت فداك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir says Jacob lived two years with Joseph and remained God's proof despite Joseph's kingship; after Jacob's death Joseph became the proof and carried his remains to Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم قال قلت لأبي جعفر عليه السلام كم عاش يعقوب مع يوسف بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author selects reports relevant to these verses and says most reports about Joseph have confused wording and weak chains.
rows.anchor: على أن أكثرها لا يخلو من تشوش في المتن وضعف في السند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete faith as pure monotheism is rare; most do not believe, and most of the few believers retain shirk, leaving very few with pure tawhid.
rows.anchor: الإيمان الكامل وهو التوحيد الخالص عزيز المنال لا يناله إلا قليل من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly absorption and neglect of innate knowledge of God explain why most will not believe, however much the Prophet wishes it.
rows.anchor: لانكبابهم على الدنيا وانجذاب نفوسهم إلى زينتها وسهوهم عما أودع في فطرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause means they disbelieve although the Prophet seeks no payment, so expense is not what prevents acceptance.
rows.anchor: الواو حالية أي ما هم بمؤمنين والحال أنك ما تسألهم على إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder that reawakens innate knowledge of God, not a commodity for wealth, status, or honor.
rows.anchor: بيان لشأن القرآن الواقعي وهو أنه ممحض في أنه ذكر للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction may be circumstantial or introductory; passing by signs means encountering them successively and moving on.
rows.anchor: والمرور على الشيء هو موافاته ثم تركه بموافاة ما وراءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavenly and earthly signs, through their existence and ordered structure, indicate God's oneness, though people ignore them.
rows.anchor: آيات كثيرة سماوية وأرضية تدل بوجودها والنظام البديع الجاري فيها على توحيد ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If passing is literal rather than figurative, the verse supports modern astronomy: Earth's rotation and orbit carry us past heavenly bodies.
rows.anchor: من الدليل على ما يبتني عليه الهيئة الحديثة من حركة الأرض وضعا وانتقالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to people in respect of faith: among the few who believe, most remain mixed with shirk.
rows.anchor: ما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم متلبسون بالشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and shirk coexist by degrees because attachment to God and created things varies in strength and relation, like relative nearness and distance.
rows.anchor: إنما يكون من جهة كونها من المعاني التي تقبل في نفسها القوة والضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hidden shirk appears when professed believers fear calamity, seek honor from others, worry over provision, or disobey while knowing God sees them.
rows.anchor: ترى من يدعى الإيمان بالله يخاف وترتعد فرائصه من أي نائبة أو مصيبة تهدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means a degree of hidden shirk that coexists with a degree of faith.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالشرك في الآية بعض مراتبه الذي يجامع بعض مراتب الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects restricting the verse to Meccan idolaters or hypocrites without evidence.
rows.anchor: فما قيل إن المراد بالمشركين في الآية مشركو مكة في غير محله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāshiya stands for an omitted enveloping punishment; baghtah means suddenness, and the last clause describes people surprised by the Hour.
rows.anchor: الغاشية صفة سادة مسد الموصوف المحذوف لدلالة كلمة العذاب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses amazement at people who ignore signs, fail to purify faith, and persist heedlessly as if secure from punishment or a sudden Hour.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للتعجيب، والمعنى أن أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After pure monotheism is shown rare and supported by cosmic signs, the Prophet is told to declare his path of calling to it with insight.
rows.anchor: أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يبين لهم أن سبيله هو الدعاء إلى هذا التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is my way announces the path; calling to God with insight explains it; Glory be to God is an interposed declaration of transcendence, and denying shirk confirms its purity.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لمعنى الدعوة إلى الله بيان أن هذه الدعوة ليست دعوة إليه تعالى كيف كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Followers share the duty of calling, but only sincere, knowledgeable people of insight share this path; not every follower qualifies.
rows.anchor: لكن السياق يدل على أن الإشراك ليس بذاك العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone heedless of God, secure from His plan, and turned from His signs cannot call others to God with insight.
rows.anchor: وكيف يدعو إلى الله من كان غافلا عنه آمنا من مكره معرضا عن آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were human men from towns, like Muhammad, who received revelation and called their people; ruined settlements attest to disbelief's outcome.
rows.anchor: لم يكن الرسل الماضون ملائكة وإنما بعثوا من بين هؤلاء الناس وكانوا رجالا من أهل القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet follows earlier messengers in calling people to fear God, which brings lasting happiness and reward in the next life.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يتقوا الله فيفلحوا ويفوزوا بسعادة خالدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling messengers townspeople emphasizes that they belonged to, lived among, and were known by their audiences, not angels or outsiders.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أنهم كانوا من أنفسهم يعيشون بينهم ومعروفين عندهم بالمعاشرة والمخالطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about traveling the earth warns Muhammad's community with the fate of earlier peoples who ignored warnings.
rows.anchor: إنذار لأمة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمثل ما أنذر به الأمم الخالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next life is better for the Godfearing; the call to piety is sincere counsel gathering all their good and happiness.
rows.anchor: بيان النصح وأن ما يدعون إليه وهو التقوى ليس وراءه إلا ما فيه كل خيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes equate yāʾisa and istayʾasa; the author allows the latter to mean nearing despair as its signs emerge, not absolute despair.
rows.anchor: وهو مما يعد يأسا عرفا وليس باليأس القاطع حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers warned the people without response until they nearly despaired of their belief, and then God's aid arrived.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من إيمان أولئك الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warnings are ignored, God grants victory to believers, and none can avert His punishment from guilty people.
rows.anchor: فلم يستجيبوا وأنذروهم بعذاب الله فلم ينتهوا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿibr means passing from one state to another, while ʿibra transfers knowledge from what is seen to what is unseen.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب أصل العبر تجاوز من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stories may refer to all the prophets, including Joseph, or possibly to Joseph and his brothers; the first is foregrounded.
rows.anchor: والضمير في قصصهم للأنبياء ومنهم يوسف صاحب القصة في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is not invented but confirms earlier scripture, especially the Torah's account, and details what people need for religious welfare and happiness.
rows.anchor: ما كان القصص المذكور في السورة حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يدي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is guidance to success and a special mercy for believers.
rows.anchor: وهدى إلى السعادة والفلاح ورحمة خاصة من الله سبحانه لقوم يؤمنون به

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir explains shirk as obedience: sins follow Satan and share obedience with God, without worshipping another deity.
rows.anchor: عن الفضيل عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā says the shirk described does not amount to disbelief.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن الفضيل عن الرضا عليه السلام قال شرك لا يبلغ به الكفر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says crediting a person alone with provision or rescue makes that person a partner in God's rule; saying God favored one through that person is acceptable.
rows.anchor: عن مالك بن عطية عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في الآية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir includes swearing by another's life among the forms of shirk discussed in the verse.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة قال سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swearing by someone besides God gives that person honor not due in their own right; reports on such examples are numerous.
rows.anchor: يعني القسم بغير الله لما فيه من تعظيمه بما لا يستحقه بذاته

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir identifies the Prophet, ʿAlī, and later Imams as those who call to God with insight.
rows.anchor: عن سلام بن المستنير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq identifies ʿAlī as the first follower in faith and confirmation, who never associated anything with God or mixed faith with shirk.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو الزبيري عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في الآية قال يعني علي أول من اتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports support the preceding explanation; naming specific people may apply the verse to particular exemplars.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذكر المصداق من باب التطبيق

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq explains subḥān Allāh as anafa, expressing God's dignified transcendence.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن الحكم قال سألت أبا عبد الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Another report from al-Ṣādiq explains subḥān Allāh as declaring God transcendent.
rows.anchor: عن هشام الجواليقي قال سألت أبا عبد الله

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the world is never without a human prophet or Imam; angels were not sent as earthly leaders or judges, but to prophets.
rows.anchor: عن السيار عن الحسن بن علي عن آبائه عن الصادق عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: At al-Maʾmūn's council, al-Riḍā says the messengers nearly despaired of their people while the people thought the messengers had lied.
rows.anchor: قال الرضا يقول الله حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من قومهم فظن قومهم أن الرسل قد كذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā's report supports the author's reading; a report that messengers thought Satan appeared as angels is unreliable.
rows.anchor: وما في بعض الروايات أن الرسل ظنوا أن الشيطان تمثل لهم في صورة الملائكة لا يعتمد عليه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says God gives a messenger serenity and gravitas, making revelation as unmistakable as what he sees with his eyes.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة قال قلت لأبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A report collected by Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir has Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read the messengers as despairing their people would believe and the people as thinking they had lied; al-Ḍaḥḥāk agrees.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم عن أبي حمزة الجزري قال صنعت طعاما فدعوت ناسا من أصحابنا منهم سعيد بن جبير والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah centers on God's transcendence of every partner; glorification recurs throughout, and its close denies child, partner, or need for a protector.
rows.anchor: تتعرض لأمر توحيده تعالى عن الشريك مطلقا ومع ذلك يغلب فيها جانب التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author regards the surah as Meccan based on its themes; its laws do not prove a Medinan setting because similar rulings occur in Meccan surahs.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية لشهادة مضامين آياتها بذلك

rows.speaker: بعضهم كما في روح المعاني
rows.claim: One view exempts two verses about nearly tempting and nearly expelling the Prophet from the Meccan classification.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم كما في روح المعاني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view exempts four verses, adding God's encompassing people and the prayer for a truthful entrance.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم إلا أربع آيات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan exempts five verses, including prohibitions on killing and fornication, the invoked beings, prayer, and giving relatives their due.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنها مكية إلا خمس آيات

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil exempts five verses: those on tempting or expelling the Prophet, God's encompassing people, the truthful-entry prayer, and those given knowledge.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل مكية إلا خمس

rows.speaker: قتادة والمعدل عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Muʿaddal, reporting from Ibn ʿAbbās, exempt eight verses from the passage about nearly tempting the Prophet through the truthful-entry prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة والمعدل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds no indication these verses are Medinan; related rulings also occur in Meccan al-Anʿām and al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة في مضامين الآيات على كونها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening describes the Prophet's night journey from the Sacred Mosque to Jerusalem's Farthest Mosque, associated with David and Solomon.
rows.anchor: فذكر اسراؤه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى وهو بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion turns to Israelite history: obedience raised them, disobedience lowered them, and God commanded monotheism and rejection of partners.
rows.anchor: فكلما أطاعوا رفعهم الله وكلما عصوا خفضهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah applies the same pattern to Muhammad's community and presents teachings on God, return, and general laws.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك جرت السنة الإلهية في الأمم الماضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author highlights verses on God's beautiful names, provision for both groups, and destruction decreed for every town.
rows.anchor: ومن غرر الآيات فيها قوله تعالى
